Lens: pre-authorization effects and registry bypass, commit 7245fa5d (PR #291), probed on real Bodies in scratch worktrees; nothing pushed, no working tree of the main checkout touched.

The two concerns the request names hold at this head. (1) `around` is applied lazily: in no ordinary path did caller code or an adapter run before the grant and the Gate's dispatch. I confirmed the PR's own cases (attach refusal, target prefix, OUTSIDE_SCOPE, NEEDS_DECISION, retained receipt, UNCERTAIN retry; 29 passed) and added policy DENY, UNAVAILABLE and a Gate identity refusal: the wrapper was never built. (2) An office without a registry runs nothing; `Body.open` is the only construction site and shares one registry with engine and Genesis. Both PR mutation gates pass (11/11, 5/5). On integration-rehearsal-20261111 (#290+#291+#273+#278) a detach landing in the background hand-off window is refused at the office and the worker never runs.

What I could break:
- In model, low, pre-existing: the separate appraiser (greg/appraisal.py) calls built-in sensor adapters directly, with no office, grant, receipt or attach check. A founder-DETACHED fs.read was executed for a pending closure.
- Outside the stated model but real, medium, pre-existing: `act` reuses a retained receipt as DONE without reading its result_class. A body killed between the Gate's negative receipt and `mission.compensated` records a refused compensation as DONE on restart and never raises the COMPENSATION ask.
- Out of model (needs in-process caller code), low: `around` lets the wrapper choose what runs. The exact #291 defect reproduces through it with an effect: founder-DETACHED internal_write `body.backup` wrote a seed under ATTACHED read-only `body.backup_status`'s grant, receipt and read_only cone. The AST allowlist that guards `around` misses 4 of 5 spellings.
- Out of model, low: the manifest identity check believes the presented object's own `digest()` and pins nothing, so a lying subclass or an in-place mutation runs an internal_write capability under a read_only cone; `adapter=None` skips the adapter check and still gets a grant and a dispatch claim.
- Test gap, low: two clauses of the new context check have no failing test (two mutants survive both authority test files).

The appraiser and compensation findings reproduce identically on pr290 and on the rehearsal branch, so neither is a regression of #291. Not runnable here: tests/unit/test_greg_recombine.py is skipped (networkx missing), so engine-detach behaviour was probed directly instead.

findings.title: A retained negative receipt is reused as DONE: a refused compensation is recorded DONE after a kill, and the founder is never asked
findings.claim: AuthorityOffice.act's reuse branch (`claim, receipt = self._prior(proposal_id)` ... `return ActionOutcome("DONE", ["retained receipt reused after restart"], ...)`) does not read the receipt's result_class; the legacy-scope branch a few lines above does. MissionEngine._run_compensation asks with a fixed attempt (`compensate:<aid>:<receipt>`), so a body killed between the Gate's negative receipt and the `mission.compensated` record asks the same proposal again on restart and gets DONE. The journal then says the compensation is DONE citing a receipt whose result is 'capability refused', the effect is not undone, and the COMPENSATION ask the unkilled path raises never appears. Strategies are not affected (`_recover_dispatch` reads result_class). Outside the lens's four outcomes (no unattached capability runs, nothing runs early), found while checking the retained-receipt path; pre-existing on pr196/pr290 and present on the rehearsal branch.

findings.claim: The office calls `around(registered)(params, ctx)` and accepts whatever callable the wrapper returns. The docstring's 'never which adapter' is not enforced. findings.title: The manifest identity check trusts the presented object's own digest() and pins nothing; a lying subclass or an in-place mutation runs an internal_write capability under a read_only cone
findings.claim: `attach_refusal` compares `registered.digest() != manifest.digest()` (the presented object answers for itself) and skips even that when `registered is manifest`. After the check, `act` keeps using the presented manifest for consequence class, target prefix, availability and the proposal's manifest_digest. A CapabilityManifest subclass that returns the registered digest, or the registered manifest mutated in place (it is a non-frozen dataclass handed to every adapter as ctx.manifest), made artifact.store (internal_write) run DONE under a read_only cone. The same objects run caller code before any grant (`digest()`, `available()`, a `ctx.manifest` property). No current code in greg/ mutates a registered manifest (grep found one pre-registration write in genesis.py:2184), so this needs hostile in-process code today.
